text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Quiet general parliamentary session reflects harmony between the country's top leaders.
- Princeton University professor John Waterbury chosen to head American University of Beirut.
- Wednesday's cabinet session to study the unification of school teachers' payscales.
- Two Hizbollah fighters killed in south Lebanon clashes. Guerrillas fired rockets into the occupation zone late on Sunday.
- Verdict in Japanese Red Army guerrillas case on July 31. Defence lawyers said the suspects had no criminal intention and MP Najah Wakim said the Lebanese authorities knew about them since 1985.
- Surplus of subscription against maturity of Lebanon treasury bills exceeds 66 billion pounds for the latest issue.
- Solidere attempts to open up subscription to foreigners.
- Hrawi told the Syrians in his latest trip to Damascus that he wanted to name a new prime minister - ministerial sources.
- Hizbollah eliminates the possibility of a widescale Israeli military operation on Lebanon.
- President Hrawi says: We will not surrender to Israeli pressures.
